1.title: The Core Workflow: init, validate, plan, apply, destroy and fmt
1.text: Welcome to Module four: The Core Workflow: init, validate, plan, apply, destroy and fmt. It covers the exam area three. Core Terraform workflow. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. three A Describe the Terraform workflow. three B Initialize a Terraform working directory. three C Validate a Terraform configuration. three D Generate and review an execution plan. three E Apply changes to infrastructure. three F Destroy Terraform-managed infrastructure. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: three. Core Terraform workflow. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: The workflow
1.text: The workflow. The figure shows this: Write, init, plan, apply: the core Terraform workflow.

1.title: The workflow, continued
1.text: The workflow. Write. Command: (an editor). What it does: Describe the infrastructure in dot tf files. Initialize. Command: terraform init. What it does: Prepare the working directory: install providers and modules, set up the backend. Validate. Command: terraform validate. What it does: Check syntax and consistency. Plan. Command: terraform plan. What it does: Preview the changes. Apply. Command: terraform apply. What it does: Make the changes. Destroy. Command: terraform destroy. What it does: Remove everything Terraform manages. Format. Command: terraform fmt. What it does: Rewrite files in the standard style. Exam tip: Write, init, plan, apply. init always comes first in a new or changed working directory.

1.title: terraform init
1.text: terraform init. terraform init initializes a working directory that contains configuration. Installs providers. Downloads them and writes dot terraform dot lock dot hcl. Downloads modules. Into dot terraform slash modules. Configures the backend. Prepares where state is stored. Is safe to repeat. Idempotent; run it again after changing providers, modules or the backend. Useful options: -upgrade (newest allowed provider versions), -reconfigure (ignore the saved backend settings), -migrate state (move state to a new backend), -backend false (skip backend setup).

1.title: terraform validate and terraform fmt
1.text: terraform validate and terraform fmt. terraform validate. Checks that the configuration is syntactically valid and internally consistent (for example references and argument names); does not contact remote services and does not check the state; run after init because it needs provider schemas. terraform fmt. Rewrites dot tf files to the canonical format and style (indentation, alignment); options -check (report only), -diff (show changes), -recursive (include subdirectories). Exam tip: validate does not check that resources can be created. It only checks the configuration itself. fmt only changes style, never meaning.

1.title: terraform plan
1.text: terraform plan. terraform plan creates an execution plan: it reads the state, refreshes it from the real infrastructure, compares the configuration with it and lists the changes it would make. It changes nothing. plus. Create. -. Destroy. about. Update in place. - or plus. Replace: destroy, then create. plus or -. Replace with create before destroy. Read a data source. -out F I L E. Save the plan to apply exactly that plan later. -destroy. Plan a destroy. -refresh only. Plan only state updates (Module fourteen). -target A D D R E S S. Limit the plan to one resource (use rarely). -var, -var file. Set input variables. -replace A D D R E S S. Force replacement of one resource.

1.title: terraform apply and terraform destroy
1.text: terraform apply and terraform destroy. terraform apply. Creates a plan, shows it and asks for confirmation (type yes ), then carries it out and updates the state. terraform apply -auto approve. Skips the prompt (for automation). terraform apply tfplan. Applies a saved plan with no prompt; the plan must still match the state. terraform destroy. Destroys all resources in the state; the same as terraform apply -destroy; asks for confirmation. Exam tip: A saved plan applies without a prompt. terraform destroy equals terraform apply -destroy. -auto approve removes the safety prompt.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A new working directory contains configuration that uses the aws provider. Which command must be run first? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: terraform init. terraform init installs the providers and prepares the backend before plan or apply.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which command shows what Terraform would change without changing anything? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: terraform plan. terraform plan creates and shows an execution plan without making changes.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. In a plan, a resource is marked - or plus. What does this mean? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The resource will be destroyed and created again. The symbol - or plus means replace: destroy then create.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team wants a pipeline to apply exactly the plan that was reviewed. What should it do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Run terraform plan -out equals tfplan and later terraform apply tfplan. A saved plan is applied exactly as reviewed, without a new prompt.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which command rewrites configuration files into the standard style? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: terraform fmt. terraform fmt reformats files to the canonical style.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which statement about terraform validate is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: It checks the configuration for syntax and internal consistency. validate checks syntax and consistency of the configuration; it does not contact remote services.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does terraform init do? Answer: Prepares the working directory: providers, modules, backend. Question two. What does plus mean in a plan? Answer: Create. Question three. What does about mean in a plan? Answer: Update in place.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is terraform destroy equal to? Answer: terraform apply -destroy. Question five. What does -auto-approve do? Answer: Skips the confirmation prompt. Question six. What does terraform fmt change? Answer: Only style, not meaning.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Workflow: write, init, plan, apply (destroy when done). init: providers, modules, backend, lock file; repeat safely; -upgrade. validate or fmt: consistency check, no remote calls or canonical style. plan symbols: plus create, - destroy, about update, - or plus replace, less than equals read. apply: prompt unless -auto-approve or saved plan.
